data.description: CLAUDE.md still describes a dead architecture (form.py, simplify.py, generate.py, dataset.py, cli.py, 'bench generate' CLI) that no longer exists. Actual code: src/lofbench/ with core.py (form repr + simplify + generate + DIFFICULTY_CONFIGS), renderers/ (registry: canonical, noisy_parens, circle, nested_list, sexpr), datasets/factory.py (inspect-ai Sample factories, handles text + image dialects), tasks/ (single.py, composite.py, prompts.py), scorers/lof_scorer.py, analysis.py (inspect log loading + pandas). Rewrite the project-overview/architecture/commands sections of CLAUDE.md to match reality; keep the Lattice section intact. README.org is mostly accurate but verify examples against current __init__.py exports. Why: agents reading stale docs hallucinate the old layout.
data.title: Refresh CLAUDE.md and README to match actual lofbench architecture

data.description: Core thesis of the bench: representation sensitivity. The calculus is trivial; the question is whether models reason over structure or over token statistics of the surface form. Add a handful of new text dialects as FormRenderer subclasses registered in renderers/__init__.py. Candidate directions (pick during planning, ~3-5): indentation/tree notation, XML/HTML-style open-close tags, JSON nesting, natural-language containment prose ('a circle containing two circles...'), emoji/unicode bracket vocabularies (notebooks/emoji-examples.txt has prior art), word-delimited brackets (BEGIN/END), whitespace-noise variants. Each renderer must be structure-preserving (isomorphic to the canonical form), deterministic under a seed, and covered by tests mirroring tests/test_renderers.py patterns. Decision context: paired design — same underlying forms across all dialects — is already the sampling strategy, so renderers must not alter form identity.
data.title: New text-structure dialects (renderers)

data.description: Extend visual dialect coverage beyond svg_circle_renderer.py. Candidates: nested boxes/rectangles, color-coded containment, hand-drawn-style jitter on circles, non-containment encodings (e.g., tree diagrams) to test whether spatial containment specifically matters. Datasets factory already handles image samples (ContentImage path in datasets/factory.py keyed on metadata format=image), so new visual renderers just need to emit that. Cost warning baked into scope: vision samples on flagship models are the budget danger zone (total out-of-pocket budget for eval runs is 100 USD) — visual dialect grids run on cheap multimodal tiers first, flagships only on a reduced grid.
data.title: New visual dialects (renderers)

data.description: Valerie wants 'more dialect transformation pipelines': the ability to compose/chain transformations rather than one monolithic renderer per dialect, e.g., sexpr base + noisy symbol substitution + whitespace noise. Design a pipeline abstraction over FormRenderer (or a transform layer between canonical form and final rendering) that keeps register_renderer/get_renderer registry compatibility so inspect task -T renderer=... params keep working (possibly a spec string or config dict for composed pipelines). Must preserve determinism under render_seed and record the full transform chain in RenderedForm.metadata so analysis can attribute effects. This unlocks the combinatorially large representation space cheaply — the point is many surface forms per identical structure.
data.title: Dialect transformation pipeline (composable renderers)

data.description: Bridge between eval runs and the public site. analysis.py already loads inspect logs into pandas; extend it into a repeatable pipeline: logs/ -> tidy per-sample records (model, dialect/renderer+config, difficulty, depth, steps, correct, tokens, cost) -> versioned parquet/json artifacts the static site consumes, plus per-sample transcript extracts for the example-walkthrough pages. Should be a CLI or single entry point so the release workflow is 'run evals, run pipeline, rebuild site'. Include paired-comparison aggregates (same form across dialects -> per-item deltas, McNemar-style tables) since paired design is the core analysis. Depends on nothing; site (DB-6) depends on this.
data.title: Results data pipeline: inspect logs to tidy site-ready data

data.description: Public static site (github pages or similar) framed around representation sensitivity, not 'can models do LoF'. Components: (1) hero charts — accuracy by model x dialect, paired deltas vs canonical; (2) methodology/axioms explainer (I1 calling, I2 crossing); (3) example walkthroughs from real transcripts (correct + failure cases); (4) an exploration sandbox: pick/enter a form, see it rendered simultaneously in every dialect — same shape, many surfaces. Decision context: Valerie explicitly wants the sandbox ('exploration of how the same shape results in many different outputs and structures'); inspect view stays a private exploration tool, the site is the publishing surface. Reference for scope/tone: cbrower.dev/vpct (single hero chart + methodology + walkthroughs). Sandbox likely needs renderers ported/compiled to JS or pre-rendered outputs for a curated form set — decide in planning. Consumes artifacts from the data-pipeline task.
data.title: Static site: representation-sensitivity showcase + dialect sandbox

data.description: Write down the measurement design so runs are defensible and affordable. Content: paired design rationale (same forms across dialects, within-item comparisons, McNemar-style tests — already the practice, needs documenting); sample size math (binary outcome, 95% CI half-width ~1/sqrt(n): n=100 -> +-10pp, n=400 -> +-5pp; paired deltas need far less); model tiering (full dialect grid on cheap tiers, reduced grid on 2-3 flagships); batch API 50% discount; vision-dialect cost gating. Hard constraint: total out-of-pocket eval budget 100 USD. Output: notebooks/measurement.org exists as prior thinking — reconcile with it, produce a doc the release skill and future runs follow.
data.title: Sampling and budget design doc (paired design, model tiers, CI math)

data.description: Release cadence is manual and event-driven (new model drops), not cron. Build a skill file usable from Claude Code or the hermes agent that walks the operator through: detect/confirm new model id + provider, run the eval grid per the sampling design doc (respecting budget guardrails and batch API), run the data pipeline, regenerate site charts, sanity-check results vs prior runs, publish. Decision context from conversation: Valerie explicitly prefers a skill-file-assisted manual flow over scheduled automation because each run costs real money and should only happen when there is news. Depends on data pipeline (DB-5) and sampling doc (DB-7) existing.
data.title: Release-cadence skill: new-model-drop to refreshed charts
lofsite sandbox fan-out breaks on spatial dialects before DB-4 M5's emit() lands

data.description:
Discovered by the DB-8 implementer's dry runs. The frozen suite (suites/v1.json, 120 forms by 29 dialects, payload hashes, rerun gate) has no eval-time consumer. single_lof_task and composite_lof_task generate forms live from a seed, so a run today produces different forms than the frozen table (verified: live lof_001 differs from suite v1's lof_001) and stamps suite_version adhoc. Until fixed, every run is pilot-grade and the headline sensitivity score cannot claim suite v1.

Scope: add a suite parameter to the tasks (for example -T suite=v1 -T dialect=parens.noisy-v1) that loads the frozen id-to-form table and the named dialect spec through the suite loader (threading suite_version into DialectSpec, which already exists in src/lofbench/suites.py), verifies payload hashes before any model call (the rerun gate), and stamps true suite provenance into sample metadata. The dataset factory path must use the frozen forms, not the generator. Also decide and record the flagship core subset (a fixed form_id list per docs/measurement-design.md section 7) inside the suite file, which the DB-8 release skill needs.

The bench-release skill (DB-8) hard-refuses v1 releases until this lands.
data.title: Suite-driven evaluation: make inspect tasks consume suites/v1.json
